report:
Fresh source assessment of crates.sage_inspector.inspection.source_evidence. The claim requires Rust-source integration inputs in a checked-in Cargo project, traversal through the production workspace host/live inspection provider/actor/Axum, output snapshots of values and demand, and exclusion of precomputed JSON or scripted semantic providers as semantic-result suppliers. The captured architectural-foundations section distinguishes focused unit tests or injected OS failures from semantic end-to-end evidence.

All three ordinary implementation entries were inspected. tests/semantic_inspector.rs::inspector_project selects test-projects/semantic-inspector/db-drop-guard. The captured Cargo.toml defines the db-drop-guard library and the captured src/lib.rs contains Db, DbDropGuard, and the db method returning self.db.clone(). src/main.rs::run_inspector opens SageHost::try_open with the working directory/package choice, constructs a LiveInspectionProvider borrowing that host, moves it into serve_actor on the database actor thread, and passes the typed InspectionClient to the production server. crates/sage-inspector/src/server.rs::run_server calls axum::serve over router(client); the actual session/symbol/product/run routes delegate to that client and encode its returned values. The captured actor dispatch calls the supplied provider and records each demand; there is no fixture JSON result injection in this path.

The current real_command_serves_embedded_assets_and_correlated_request_logs scenario launches CARGO_BIN_EXE_cargo-sage with sage inspect --port 0 --no-open in that Cargo project. It extracts the actual readiness URL, sends TCP HTTP requests, derives the selected method path, advertised identity URL and run identifier from returned responses, and asserts protocol version, local root, db label, product title and run kind. It snapshots the real revision/identity/error responses and constructs the visible-summary/demand snapshot from live response values and inspection-request events read from child stderr. The twelve-event length and exact request/operation/argument/status/run snapshot make the demand observations concrete. Expected snapshots are only comparison targets; neither those strings nor a scripted semantic provider supplies the responses. Asset/fallback and occupied-port assertions are transport/OS boundary checks, not substitutes for semantic execution.

Other supplied source-driven scenarios open the same project using run_sage_host_with and LiveInspectionProvider. real_symbol_index_is_complete_local_and_detail_free inspects returned labels, reflection shapes and cold/warm query demand. edit_matrix_distinguishes_relevant_execution_from_unrelated_validation changes source through FileUpdate, compares before/after typed-IR values, and asserts executed-body versus validated work. retained_host_separates_edits_from_demand_and_preserves_symbol_paths tests live edits and source-derived references. These show meaningful partial backend evidence; they do not by themselves establish a complete browser UI acceptance scenario. Synthetic tracked-query probes and FakeWatcher unit tests do not masquerade as source-derived semantic integration results.

The entire formally associated test set consists of sage_meta::todo::crates_sage_inspector_inspection_source_evidence. Its body has no assertions. Its explicit prerequisite is to associate and review complete backend and browser integration evidence that launches the real command over the same sample, drives production routes, snapshots returned values/visible UI/actor-query demand, and demonstrates source edits taking effect only through the live database. I accept this as a visible evidence-completion deferral: the existing command and provider scenarios are substantive partial support, but the TODO is not counted as passing behavioral verification, and full browser/source-edit integration coverage is not approved as complete. No N/A entries exist. All claim requirements have either concrete source-path support above or remain within that explicit comprehensive-evidence TODO. I found no contradictory precomputed semantic-result supplier in the reviewed paths and request no changes for this refresh.

This refresh executed review start/read and source inspection only, followed by review record; it made no Rust edits and ran no behavioral tests or build. Central test execution is assigned to the coordinator, and no earlier test result or prior verdict is used as current execution evidence. Dependencies used for this judgment were captured with review read, including the checked-in fixture, actor dispatch, source-evidence rationale and review-decision rule.
